title: On a computer, the AI side panel cannot be reached or closed well with the keyboard
what: Pressing the AI Assistant button opens the side panel, but the keyboard focus does not move into it: the button disappears and the focus drops to the top of the page, so a keyboard or screen-reader user has to hunt for the panel. Escape does not close it, and after closing it the focus is lost again instead of going back to the button.
expected: Opening the panel puts the focus in its ask box, Escape closes it, and closing it returns the focus to the AI Assistant button.
who: owners who use a keyboard or screen reader on a computer
how_often: every time the panel opens or closes
fix_line: Move the focus into the panel when it opens, close it on Escape, and give the focus back to the button on close

title: A screen reader hears 'Thinking' but never hears that the answer has come
what: While the assistant works, a 'Thinking' line is announced. When the answer card arrives that line just vanishes and the card is not announced, and the focus stays in the ask box. A blind owner does not know the answer is there or where it is.
expected: When the answer arrives, a short line such as 'Answer ready' is announced, or the card's heading is announced.
fix_line: Announce the answer's arrival in a polite live line when the Thinking line goes away

title: Member names in an answer and past tasks in History can be tapped but look like plain text
what: In an answer card, each member's name opens that member, and in History each past task puts its words back in the box. Both are drawn as plain text with no border, arrow or colour, so a first-time owner does not know they can tap them. The picture of the member list shows two plain names.
expected: Rows that open something show a small arrow (as other lists in the panel do) or a clear row look, and History says 'Tap to ask again'.
how_often: every member list answer and every History visit
fix_line: Add the panel's usual arrow to these rows and a short hint on History

title: When today's questions are used up, the only reason shown is faint grey text inside a locked box
what: At the daily limit the ask box, the microphone and the send button all turn off. The only words saying why are the box's greyed placeholder; no line above the box says it (the 'questions left' line stops at 1). A screen reader reads only 'Ask or give a task, dimmed', and greyed placeholder text in a locked box is hard to read in both colour schemes.
expected: A plain line above the box says that today's free questions are used up and when they come back, read out by a screen reader.
who: owners who hit the daily limit, worst for screen-reader users
how_often: every time the limit is reached
fix_line: Show the limit line as real text above the box when it is locked

title: Closing the voice sheet after speaking throws away what was heard
what: After the owner speaks, the sheet shows the words it heard to fix. Cancel, Escape or a tap outside closes it and the words are gone. Opening it again starts the microphone afresh, so the owner must speak again, which uses more of the day's voice minutes.
expected: Closing after the words are heard keeps them, for example by putting them in the ask box, so nothing spoken is lost.
how_often: whenever the voice sheet is closed after speaking
fix_line: On close, put the heard words in the ask box instead of dropping them

title: A changed member AI switch or monthly limit is lost without a word if the credits sheet is closed
what: In AI credits, the owner can turn members' AI answers on or off and change the monthly limit, then must press Save changes. Closing the sheet with the cross, Escape or a tap outside throws the change away with no warning, so the owner may think members' AI is off when it is still on.
expected: Closing with an unsaved change asks 'Save your change?' or keeps the change until saved.
how_often: whenever the sheet is closed before saving
fix_line: Ask before closing when the switch or limit changed and was not saved

title: Several AI Assistant buttons are smaller than the panel's own finger-size rule
what: The panel's rule is 44 points for anything tapped. In the assistant the credits pill and the Ask/History tabs are 36, the 'Open Members' style links 32, the language and Now/Later choices 34, member rows in an answer 36, the small rewrite chips 36 and the panel's close cross 40.
expected: Every tap target is at least 44 points high, like the rest of the panel.
fix_line: Raise these controls to the panel's 44-point minimum

title: The ask box shows no focus ring when reached with the keyboard
what: The ask box turns off the browser's focus outline and its frame does not change when it has the focus, so a keyboard user cannot see that the box is selected until typing starts.
expected: The ask box's frame lights up in the accent colour when it has the keyboard focus, like other focus rings in the panel.
fix_line: Show an accent frame on the ask box while it has the focus

title: No automatic accessibility check ever looks at the AI Assistant
what: The panel's automatic accessibility crawl visits the assistant's address, but the demo gym has the assistant off, so it only sees the Today page it falls back to. The assistant's own test takes pictures in dark and light but runs no accessibility check. Contrast, labels and roles in the assistant are never measured.
expected: The accessibility check runs on the assistant's main screen, its cards and its sheets in dark and light.
fix_line: Run the accessibility check inside the assistant's existing picture test

title: Closing the side panel throws away a half-typed request
what: Words typed in the ask box live only while the panel is open. Closing the panel with the cross, or leaving the full-screen assistant on a phone, empties the box; the chat itself is kept.
expected: A half-typed request is still in the box when the owner opens the assistant again.
how_often: whenever the panel is closed mid-typing
fix_line: Keep the box's words with the chat so they survive closing
